newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt alerted to 97 deficit cut risks - paper.
newsitem.headline: French govt alerted to 97 deficit cut risks - paper.

text.p: French afternoon daily Le Monde said on Wednesday the finance ministry's budget and forecasting divisions had alerted the government to threats to the goal of cutting the public deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997.

As the government prepares for a parliamentary debate on the 1998 budget in May, Le Monde said simulations carried out by the divisions of the finance ministry pointed to potential risks of a fairly significant overshoot in 1997 without corrective steps.
It highlighted that the government was committed to meeting the three percent target in 1997 and doing all that was needed. Further measures might be required to meet this, Le Monde said.

"According to our information, the budget and forecasting services of the finance ministry -- the former in a more alarmist tone -- have presented simulations to the government which hint that France could quite markedly overshoot the three percent deficit target with unchanged policy," it said.

Among the risks referred were weak revenues, notably weak value-added tax receipts in the last months of 1996 and early months of 1997, signs of growth based more on foreign than domestic demand as well as the social security deficit.
The newspaper said this kind of warning was traditional at this time of year -- ahead of 1998 budget debate.
It said the spending side of public finances was looking good and that the risk was on the revenue side.

The paper said "reliable sources" had told it that the government's deficit reduction programme had been based on an expectation that the wage bill would progress by around four percent this year, but that the trend at the moment looked headed for a rise limited to around three percent.
The government was counting on a social security deficit of 30 billion francs but the wage trend risked increasing this.
"If this (wage) trend proved more lasting, the lost revenues for the social security could be around 10 or 12 billion."

Prime Minister Alain Juppe met heads of French political parties and the parliament's influential finance committee for lunch on Tuesday in preparation for the 1998 budget debate in the National Assembly on May 13-14.
Juppe confirmed Finance Minister Jean Arthuis's plan, announced on March 6, to freeze about 10 billion francs of 1997 spending credits as a precaution against budgetary overshoot.
"But in government circles, people are not hiding the fact it may be necessary to consider turning the screws further, if there is slippage in the next two months," Le Monde said.

It said the victims of further belt-tightening could include plans by Labour Minister Jacques Barrot to extend to other low wage sectors a textile industry scheme which allows employers to contribute less in payroll charges.
